hard_spots.kind: long cumulative sentences and ruby glosses
hard_spots.why_hard: p8 is one great breath of family laughter; p16 circles with commas and repetition. Chopping into tidy English rationalises the drift, but English breath still needs breaks. Ruby gives readings that change nuance: 怜悧《れいり》, 微笑《ほゝゑみ》, 自然《ひとりで》(= on its own, not 'nature'), 茫然《ぼんやり》, 希《のぞ》み. Translate sense, do not transliterate ruby.

hard_spots.kind: sensory wording that must not become symbol
hard_spots.why_hard: Potato is 凍ったかのやうに固くざくざく, 無味な、かかはりのない冷やかな不味さ. ざくざく is gritty/crunchy hardness, not mealy. かかはりのない means unrelated / having nothing to do with her — the point is its cold ordinariness. Lingering or ennobling it turns it into a symbol the text refuses.

なつかしみと許し and 安らかさ / 安息 recur as a thinking network. 懐しみ is nostalgia/longing for what is past made dear, not homesickness. 許し is forgiveness/pardon. 安息 / 安らかさ is rest/peace, close to but not naming death. Varying them for elegance or clarifying into heaven/old age/premonition would moralise the story.

Child is 女の子 but called 坊や by both parents; English 'boy/sonny' creates a contradiction Japanese passes over. うまうまうまうま with spoon-banging is a nursing baby's 'yum-yum' / food-cry, not words. Needs a neutral warm rendering plus a note, not a quiet fix.

Twice asked why she is silent, she answers with time ('only a short time since we married' / 'only three years') and an unspoken 'large hope she herself does not understand'. Do not bridge into shared understanding; the gap between her far picture and his practical reply is structural.

motifs.english: Keep one plain storm throughout: 'storm' for 嵐, 'sound of rain and wind' for 雨風の音. Let it arrive, disappear under family noise, return to her alone, and close the book, without making it ominous.
motifs.why: Ring-composition: announced in the dark, drowned by lively confusion, heard again by mother alone at the vision, whispered by father over cleared table. It is the world continuing outside the lit room, literal as well as figurative night.

motifs.english: Keep one family of smile-words: smile for 微笑/笑み, laughter for 笑ひ where noisy. Do not vary to grin/beam/smirks. The same smile links present joy and far stillness.
motifs.why: Deliberate network: parents smile over baby now, figures only go on smiling then. Varying destroys the link between warm now and quiet then.

motifs.english: Keep 'far' / 'distant' for every 遠い form, and 'picture' for 絵. She looks at a far place, sees a distant dim picture at the bottom of her eyes and through to the future.
motifs.why: The vision's strangeness is that it is present and distant at once, seen in the same seat. Do not locate it as heaven or memory.

motifs.english: Keep one set: 'quiet' for 静か, 'peace / peaceful' for 安らかさ, 'rest' for 安息. Use the same English each recurrence so the reader hears the return.
motifs.why: Carries the temperature from tired present through vision to final stillness. Elegant variation would flatten the argument that now will become then.

motifs.english: Render なつかしみ consistently as 'nostalgia' (or 'fond longing for what is past' if glossed once) and 許し as 'forgiveness'. Never substitute affection/pardon/mercy in later occurrences.
motifs.why: The story thinks by returning to the same two words: all things will be changed into nostalgia and forgiveness. New synonyms make it sound like new thoughts.

motifs.english: Keep tiredness words together: 'weary / weariness', 'tired', 'drooping'. Preserve the mismatch: no wrinkles yet, but old fatigue.
motifs.why: Text insists twice no wrinkle has come, then loads both bodies with hollow/drooping fatigue. That mismatch is what the potato detonates; ennobling or victimising the parents loses it.

motifs.english: Keep flat repetition: 'day by day' for 一日々々, 'long' for ながい, 'only three years' / 'barely three years'. Leave p14 standing alone as its own paragraph.
motifs.why: Her distortion (a long life already lived, feeling quite old) is measured by the flat correction: barely three years of marriage. Softening that sentence into reflection removes the measure, as does varying 'long'.

narration.english_tense: past as default for the supper action, keeping the vision and its law in the same past-reported present the Japanese uses; do not shift the vision into a separate timeless present or a conditional future that decides what it is
narration.frame: single evening: a small lit room during a storm outside; outwardly nothing changes except serving, feeding, clearing and nursing, while the mother slips inwardly to a far time and returns to practical resolve
narration.narrator: third-person narrator staying close to the young couple, moving most deeply into the wife's interior in p10–p20; sees outward actions plainly and reports her picture and general law in her grammar without certifying what it is
narration.tense_habits: lyrical Taisho past with continuatives (〜てゐた, 〜ている, 〜であった) and present-like general statements; vision passages lengthen into circling present-tense description inside past narration
timeline: p1 dark outside door, storm heard
p2–p9 family gathers at low table under dim lamp; baby bangs spoon, dishes moved under table, rice served, noisy absorption drowns storm
p10–p15 mother serving stew tastes gritty tasteless potato, falls silent, looks far away; rehearses three years of poverty, fear, illness already dreamlike and dear
p16–p17 inner picture: three people in faint dim light in endless quiet story; widening thought that life will pass and be changed into nostalgia and forgiveness before rest like night
p18–p20 she sighs alone, cannot answer husband's 'why silent', hears storm again, smiles at 'what is a day's suffering'
p21–p34 evaded dialogue about only three years, large unspoken hope; husband's practical reply (two years gone, baby will walk, just a little longer); baby cries umma-umma, they lay down chopsticks
p35–p38 resolve to work, clear up, sleep and rise early; child asleep at breast, stillness, father's whisper 'storm'

data.say: This is a single-evening story whose translation stands or falls on holding two times in one prose: the small, poor, noisy present and the mother's dim, still, forgiven far-off time. I am most unsure where English must leave the vision open (three figures, that day, rest like night) without sounding evasive; the margin should say so rather than choose.

style_sheet.annotation_density: sparse; note only what the sentence cannot give: 坊や vs 女の子, アルミ鍋 period poverty, うまうま babble, the 嵐 ring. Never note what context supplies, and never use a note to decode the vision
style_sheet.author_voice: lyrical Taisho prose: soft, lingering, sentimental without irony; long cumulative sentences that drift rather than argue; plain concrete nouns for poor things beside abstract nouns (nostalgia, forgiveness, peace). Resist both drying it out and perfuming it; let flat repetition carry feeling
style_sheet.honorifics_and_names: no surnames or given names in text; keep kinship/outward labels as 'the young father' / 'the young mother' / 'the husband' / 'the wife' where Japanese varies 男/父/夫 and 女/母/彼女 — do not normalise to he/she throughout or to modern Mum/Dad. For 坊や versus 女の子 preserve the fork with a note; do not silently fix to 'girl' or 'boy'
style_sheet.keep_in_japanese: nothing in romanised body except the baby's うまうま if rendered as 'umma-umma' with a note; render 坊や in English (e.g. 'baby' / 'little one') but flag the literal 'boy' sense in the margin rather than keeping Boy as a name
style_sheet.quotation: Japanese 『』 for speech and ひとり言 to English double quotes; keep husband's two 'why are you silent' and closing soliloquy-like lines as direct speech on their own lines
style_sheet.register: plain literary English, slightly older in feel but prose a good writer would sign; baby scenes warm and concrete, vision passages slow and unadorned; no dialect, no modern slang, no elegant synonyms for repeated words
style_sheet.ruby_and_italics: source 《》 are reading glosses, not emphasis: 卓《テーブル》 = table, 自然《ひとりで》 = on its own, etc. Render sense in plain type; do not use italics to carry strangeness unless for the baby's babble if needed
